name: Wayfinch AI
tagline: Find the right AI tool. Then learn the route.
positioning: Wayfinch AI is the field guide for non-technical people who want to pick one AI tool for a real task and learn it through short, numbered tutorial trails instead of hype-driven lists.
audience: Curious beginners, freelancers, teachers and small-team operators who feel overwhelmed by the number of AI tools and want plain-language guidance tied to everyday tasks.
strategy: Organise discovery by task, not by hype: a filterable directory where every tool listing links to a step-by-step trail. Build trust with a transparent review method and privacy-first questions, then grow community through free live 'Tool Walk' sessions and a weekly newsletter.

contrastPairs.use: text on yellow panels and highlights
text on orange chips, step numbers and CTA
small orange labels on paper (darkened orange)

designSystem.spacing: 8px base grid; 24/48/96px section rhythm; 64px minimum safe margin on social canvases
designSystem.radius: 16-22px on cards, fully rounded pills for chips and buttons, 36-40px on map panels
designSystem.borders: 3px Night Map outlines on cards with a solid 8px offset shadow, like a printed field-guide catalog
designSystem.imagery: Original inline SVG only: topographic contour lines, dotted routes, map pins, compass roses and the finch mark; no photos
designSystem.shapes: Teardrop map pins, numbered circles, organic 'region' blobs, rounded directory cards
designSystem.buttons: Pill buttons; primary Compass Blue with white label, secondary Finch Orange with ink label and ink outline
designSystem.cards: White tool cards with ink outline, offset shadow, category chip, learning-curve dots and a 'Wayfinch take' line
designSystem.motifs: Finch mark, dotted map routes connecting numbered tutorial steps, tool directory cards, filter chips

artDirection: Every creative reads like a page from a friendly trail guide: warm paper background, Night Map ink, and one bold Compass Blue or Night Map block for weight. A dotted Finch Orange route should always lead the eye from headline to content to CTA, with numbered stops when steps are involved. Keep headlines short and set in Archivo Black, supporting copy in Archivo, and show the finch somewhere as the guide. Tool names are always fictional and framed as examples, never endorsements.
